title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
goal: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.
steps: 1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed. Three Worlds — widen gaze.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next. Three Worlds — challenge answer.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy. Three Worlds — next action.

title: ADD THE PREFIX
goal: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
steps: 1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed. Add Prefix — breathe naturally.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority. Add Prefix — pick action.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby. Add Prefix — next action.

title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
goal: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
steps: 1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent. Thanks Mind — move slowly.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move. Thanks Mind — split duty.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract. Thanks Mind — next action.

title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.
steps: 1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen. Thought Departures — soften shoulders.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object. Thought Departures — allow opposite.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station. Thought Departures — next action.

title: ENTER THE ACTION
goal: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
steps: 1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity. Enter Action — feel support.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself. Enter Action — allow opposite.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target. Enter Action — next action.

title: EMOTION, COMPLETE YOUR ARC
goal: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.
steps: 1. Locate Emotion — Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name. Emotion Complete — loosen hands.
2. Permit — Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
3. Track Sensation — Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools. Emotion Complete — notice detail.
4. Follow Appears — Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires. Emotion Complete — next action.

title: ONE CLEAN WISH
goal: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
steps: 1. Bring Person — Bring the person to mind at a safe distance. Clean Wish — widen gaze.
2. Keep It Honest — Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.
3. State Boundary — Then state the boundary or action you still need. Clean Wish — split duty.
4. Keep Discernment — Warmth does not cancel discernment. Clean Wish — next action.

title: THE 2% SOFTENING
goal: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.
steps: 1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent. Softening Still — soften shoulders.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while looking at one neutral object. Softening Still — name sensation.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch. Softening Still — next action.

title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
steps: 1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once. Play Body — hear sound.
2. Run Order — Perform A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Perform C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up. Play Body — name sensation.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop. Play Body — next action.

title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
goal: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
steps: 1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement. Four Letter — feel support.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse. Four Letter — name feeling.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters. Four Letter — next action.

title: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
goal: A large release can become several manageable ones.
steps: 1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between. Exhale Chapters — breathe naturally.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty. Exhale Chapters — name sensation.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it. Exhale Chapters — next action.

title: LET THE FIELD SELF-PUBLISH
goal: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
steps: 1. Open Field — Open Field with sight, sound, sensation, and thought available at once. Let Field — widen gaze.
2. Whatever — Notice whatever becomes prominent, then what replaces it.
3. Let All Arrive — Do not select, rank, or hold any item. Let Field — allow opposite.
4. Track Changing — Track the changing editorial order for one minute. Let Field — next action.

title: NO FAVOURITE SENSATION
goal: Receive what arrives without keeping or ejecting it.
steps: 1. Let Field — Let the field choose its next foreground. No Favourite — soften shoulders.
2. Pleasant — Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
3. Include Movement — When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too. No Favourite — notice detail.
4. End Whole — End by noticing the whole room at once. No Favourite — next action.

title: THE SENSE ROLL CALL
goal: Make the present answer in specifics.
steps: 1. Find Five — Find five distinct colours or shapes, four contact sensations, three separate sounds, two scents, and one taste or mouth sensation. Sense Roll — feel support.
2. Answer Blue — No generic answers; ‘blue attention’ beats ‘something blue.’ Let the inventory end with the most stable item. Answer Blue next. Sense Roll — name sensation. Sense Roll — next action.

title: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
goal: Meet the experience before trying to change the forecast.
steps: 1. Recognise — Recognise what is here. Rain Without — breathe naturally.

4. Experience — Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move R — Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter. Rain Without — next action.

title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
goal: Walking can become a moving attention track.
steps: 1. Place Weight — Slow enough to distinguish lift, travel, place, and weight transfer. Four Parts — move slowly.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing. Four Parts — notice detail.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact. Four Parts — next action.

title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
goal: The disappearance is part of the Notice.
steps: 1. Play Safe — Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound. Listen Past — loosen hands.
2. Follow Decay — Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay Silence — Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone. Listen Past — notice detail.
4. Let Surroundings — Let the next surroundings sound end the practice. Listen Past — next action.

title: NOTICE THE NOTICING

steps: 1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation. Notice Noticing — widen gaze.

4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact. Notice Noticing — next action.

title: THE BREATH HINGE
goal: Rest where one phase becomes another.
steps: 1. Follow Inhale — Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale. Breath Hinge — soften shoulders.
2. Leave Hinge Free — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Change — Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation. Breath Hinge — name sensation.
4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched. Breath Hinge — next action.

title: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
goal: Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.
steps: 1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound. Where Sound — hear sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable. Where Sound — notice detail.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly. Where Sound — next action.

title: THE BODY AS INNER SPACE
goal: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
steps: 1. Imagine Torso — Imagine the torso and limbs as volumes containing room rather than dense objects. Body As — breathe naturally.
2. Cavities — Notice cavities, distances, and open intervals inside the body mental picture while maintaining feet, seat, and external orientation in space. Body As — name sensation.
3. Keep Image — Keep the image gentle and anatomically nonliteral. Body As — next action.

title: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
goal: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
steps: 1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom. Catch Wanting — move slowly.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’. Catch Wanting — notice detail.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation. Catch Wanting — next action.

title: WATCH PLEASURE LEAVE CLEANLY
goal: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.
steps: 1. Choose Mild — Choose a mild enjoyable sensation. Watch Pleasure — widen gaze.
2. Track Rise — Track its rise, fullness, thinning, and the eventual return to neutral.
3. Resist — Resist grabbing for a second dose during the fading phase. Watch Pleasure — notice detail.
4. Pleasant — Notice what remains when the pleasant signal is gone. Watch Pleasure — next action.

WATCH PLEASURE LEAVE CLEANLY

1–2 minutes · Guided reset

GOAL
The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.

1. Choose Mild — Choose a mild enjoyable sensation. Watch Pleasure — widen gaze.
2. Track Rise — Track its rise, fullness, thinning, and the eventual return to neutral.
3. Resist — Resist grabbing for a second dose during the fading phase. Watch Pleasure — notice detail.
4. Pleasant — Notice what remains when the pleasant signal is gone. Watch Pleasure — next action.

WIN
✓ The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Mild → Track Rise → Resist → Pleasant

PAUSE
Avoid using this to restrict nourishment or healthy enjoyment.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
goal: Release both hands of mental grasping.
steps: 1. Check The Pull — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away. Against Still — press feet.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval. Against Still — split duty.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion. Against Still — next action.

title: STAY AT THE SENSE DOOR
goal: What you notice can occur without being kidnapped by the object.
steps: 1. Choose Sound — Choose one sound or sight. Stay At — move slowly.
2. Sensory — Notice the first sensory contact, then keep attention at the doorway of hearing or seeing rather than following associations outward. Stay At — name sensation.
3. Return Bare — When the mind travels to the object’s story, return to bare contact. Stay At — next action.

title: WHO RECEIVED THAT THOUGHT?
goal: Turn inquiry toward the assumed owner.
steps: 1. Ask Whom — When a thought appears, ask ‘To whom did this occur?’ If ‘me’ arises, ask ‘What is this me before the answer?’ Refuse biography, role, body description, and philosophy. Who Received — move slowly.
2. Hold Question — Stay with the question’s open edge for several heartbeats. Hold Question next. Who Received — notice detail. Who Received — next action.

title: REMOVE THE NAME BADGES
goal: See what remains when roles clock out briefly.
steps: 1. Name — Name the roles active today. Remove Name — move slowly.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper. Remove Name — notice detail.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next. Remove Name — next action.

title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
goal: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
steps: 1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally. Do Replace — breathe naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction. Do Replace — pick action.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over. Do Replace — next action.

title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
goal: Another thought is not free when it spends the next three minutes of your life.
steps: 1. Name Lap — Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only. Pay Next — hear sound.
2. Price Trade — Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. Buy Three — If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now. Pay Next — notice detail.
4. Close Toll — When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go. Pay Next — next action.

title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
goal: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
steps: 1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then. Put Memory — hear sound.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now. Put Memory — name feeling.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’. Put Memory — next action.

PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE

about 1 minute · Guided reset

GOAL
Grammar can accidentally keep history live.

1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then. Put Memory — hear sound.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now. Put Memory — name feeling.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’. Put Memory — next action.

WIN
✓ Grammar can accidentally keep history live.

FORMULA FLOW
Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment

title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
goal: Put the real years back between then and now.
steps: 1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together. Put Years — soften shoulders.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now. Put Years — pick action.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored. Put Years — next action.

title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
goal: Identity verbs can turn weather into a prison.
steps: 1. Drop Identity Verb — Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is. Delete Am — press feet.
2. Use Temporary — Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’. Delete Am — name feeling.
3. Add Condition — Add one condition under which the process changes. Delete Am — next action.

title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
goal: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.
steps: 1. Describe Event — Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’. Third Person — breathe naturally.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you genuinely own: ‘I will…’. Third Person — pick action.
4. Distance — Distance the content, not agency. Third Person — next action.

title: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
goal: Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
steps: 1. Sort Identity Costs — Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME. Price Keeping — loosen hands.
2. Fill The Buckets — Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets. Price Keeping — pick action.
3. Find The Price — Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep. Price Keeping — next action.

title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
goal: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
steps: 1. Give Self — Give each self-state a seat. Call Inner — feel support.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time. Call Inner — pick action.
4. Chair — The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need. Call Inner — next action.

3. Keep Words — Keep their words believable. Add Witness — next action.

title: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
goal: Different uncertainties require different responses.
steps: 1. Classify — Categorise the unknown: answerable now, answerable later, influenceable but unknowable, or permanently unknowable. Species Unknown — feel support.
2. Apply Move — Apply its matching move—research, schedule, act on influence, or practise acceptance. Species Unknown — allow opposite.
3. Use Category — Refuse to use one category’s tool on another. Species Unknown — next action.

title: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES
goal: Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.
steps: 1. Choose Plausible — Choose two plausible outcomes and build a short branch for each: first signal, first action, resource, and exit. Plan Both — loosen hands.
2. Prepare Both — Prepare any step useful in both branches now. Plan Both — allow opposite.
3. Select Path — Delay preference until evidence selects the path. Plan Both — next action.
